newsitem.title: UK: UK grains crop growth generally good, HGCA said.
newsitem.headline: UK grains crop growth generally good, HGCA said.

text.p: The general picture for developing grains crops throughout the UK is fairly optimistic, "with one of the best Autumn drilling seasons behind us," according to the UK's Home Grown Cereals Authority.

In its Weekly Digest, the HGCA says that warm and showery weather in the early autumn helped establish vigorous growth in cereal crops, resulting in good initial establishment for most crops, except oilseed rape in some areas.
However, the recent cold and frosty weather has slowed development and could even knock some crops back.
The frosty weather has helped check the development of pests.

Oilseed rape "got off to a reasonable start in most areas," the HGCA said. But crops in some parts of the Midlands and the East of England, where seedbeds were dry suffered from uneven germination and some fields were re-drilled, the authority said.
